The first objective is to facilitate access to SERV services. The second is to reduce the administrative burden. The third concerns the introduction and adjustment of products, which the revision aims to simplify. There are therefore three operational levers: access, compliance requirements and products. The communication links them to the possibility for SERV to tailor its intervention more precisely to the needs of Switzerland’s export-oriented economy.
For those observing the national economy, the documented point is the scope of the intervention: the source speaks of how the services operate and of the response to the needs of the exporting economy. However, it does not quantify the extent of the administrative reduction, list specific products or indicate amounts or deadlines. The text therefore describes what the revision aims to achieve, not a measure already implemented or a verified result. The fundamental mandate of SERV, the source specifies, remains unchanged. ## Two levels to distinguish The source allows a clear comparison between what the revision seeks to change and what it states it will leave unchanged. At the first level are access to benefits, administrative burdens, and the introduction or adjustment of products. At the second is SERV’s fundamental mandate: to preserve and create jobs and promote Switzerland as a business location.
| Area | What the source indicates | |---|---| | Access | Facilitate access to SERV benefits | | Administration | Reduce administrative burdens | | Products | Simplify introduction and adjustment | | Mandate | Preserve and create jobs; promote Switzerland as a business location |
The comparison does not measure a before and after: the communication does not provide initial values, expected values, or a measurement period. It does, however, make it possible to distinguish the revision of the instruments from the mandate. In editorial terms, the text presents an intervention concerning usability and the adaptation of the offering, not a redefinition of the stated purpose.
This distinction is relevant for a national reading. The relationship made explicit by the source moves from operational simplification to a more targeted response to the needs of the Swiss export-oriented economy. The effect on individual entities, sectors, or numerical results is not documented, however. The reference to jobs is part of the fundamental mandate, not an estimate of new employment generated by the revision. ## The informational limit of the communication The external communication contains a stated direction, but not an operational timeline. It does not indicate an effective date, an implementation deadline, amounts, estimates or percentages. Nor does it specify which services or products will be affected by the simplification. Therefore, based solely on the elements provided, it is possible to describe the objective of the revision, but not to quantify the change for the Swiss export-oriented economy.
The reference to SERV has national significance because the source explicitly links its ability to respond to the needs of the Swiss export-oriented economy. The same passage places this function alongside the mandate to preserve and create jobs and promote the Swiss business location. However, the source does not provide data on the number of jobs affected, the value of exports or the cost of administrative burdens. Nor does it document any change already implemented.
The distinction between objective and result avoids attributing to the revision effects that the text does not measure. As of October 21, 2026, the available material therefore makes it possible to record a partial revision focused on three areas — access, burdens and products — and a confirmation of the fundamental mandate. item.title: Return to standard time: clocks go back on October 25
item.description: Between October 24 and 25 standard time returns At 3 the hands turn back one hour 71% of Forsa respondents want to abolish the change Sleep
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Between October 24 and 25, standard time returns - At 3, the clock hands move back one hour - 71% of Forsa respondents want to abolish the time change - Sleep and energy remain the most debated points
## Key facts - When → night between Saturday 24 and Sunday 25 October - Operation → at 3, one hour back - Transition → from daylight saving time to Central European Time - Finding → 71% consider the change unnecessary - Contested objective → energy savings
### The return to standard time
LUGANO – In the night between Saturday 24 October and Sunday 25 October, at three in the morning, the clocks will be set back one hour. The transition will mark the return from daylight saving time to Central European Time, also referred to as standard time or normal time. It will be light earlier in the morning, while darkness will arrive earlier in the afternoon.
The most immediate result will be an extra hour of sleep for those who can take advantage of it. The same change, however, will mean one less hour of light in the evening. The source describes this very dual effect as the starting point for the new controversies: the time change continues to divide opinion, and many people are calling for its abolition.
The fact that people can sleep longer on Sunday has not made either the adoption of daylight saving time in spring or the return to standard time in autumn popular. A recent survey by the Forsa institute indicates that 71% of respondents consider the time change unnecessary and would like it abolished. This percentage reflects the respondents' views; it does not indicate that abolition has already been decided.
The text presents two categories of objections. Some people point to health consequences, particularly sleep disorders. Critics also question whether moving the clock hands achieves its original objective, namely energy savings. The discussion therefore starts from a concrete, date-specific operation but broadens to its effects on rest and the difficulty of demonstrating the energy benefit. Calls for abolition are reported as part of the debate, not as an outcome already formalized in the text. ## The comparison between light and consumption
### The original idea behind the time change
The reason cited by the source is the original goal of saving energy. Introducing daylight saving time in spring was supposed to reduce electricity consumption during the brighter months. The intended mechanism was straightforward: by moving the hands forward one hour, natural light would be used more and reliance on artificial lighting would be reduced.
The return in autumn makes the other side of the calendar visible. With the hands moved back, morning becomes light earlier, but darkness arrives earlier in the afternoon. Sunday offers an extra hour of sleep, while the evening loses an hour of light. The source thus presents the time change as a trade-off between different periods of daylight, not as a change limited to the clock face.
| Phase | Movement of the hands | Effect indicated by the source | |---|---|---| | Spring | One hour forward | Greater use of natural light and less reliance on artificial lighting | | Autumn | One hour back | More light in the morning, earlier darkness in the afternoon |
The comparison also clarifies why the energy goal is at the center of the criticism. The initial logic links natural light to less use of artificial lighting; however, the analyses cited in the text consider the actual benefits in terms of energy savings difficult to demonstrate. The source provides neither a percentage reduction in consumption nor an amount of electricity saved. For this reason, the benefit remains framed as the original goal and not as a quantified result.
The issue of light therefore does not coincide with that of sleep. In the first case, the question concerns the possibility of reducing artificial lighting; in the second, it concerns the rhythm and duration of rest. Keeping the two levels distinct avoids presenting the extra hour on Sunday as evidence of an energy benefit or, conversely, treating doubts about consumption as evidence of sleep disturbances. In the text, the two arguments remain connected by the movement of the clock hands, but are discussed separately. ## The sleep perspective
### Light as a regulator of the rhythm
In the debate, numerous sleep specialists argue for maintaining standard time, or winter time, because switching from one time schedule to another could alter the rhythm and duration of rest. According to this position, standard time better respects the balance between sleep and wakefulness.
Among the elements that regulate the biological clock and the sleep-wake rhythm, the source points to natural light, with particular reference to the blue component of sunlight. The experts cited believe that winter time preserves this balance better; the switch to daylight saving time, on the other hand, is associated with a possible lack of sleep.
The consequences indicated in the text are declines in concentration and performance, together with an increased risk of accidents. These effects are presented within the framework of the sleep specialists' arguments. However, the source does not provide a quantification for the individual episode, nor does it measure the extent of the disturbances or any possible increase in risk.
### What remains open
The cited survey offers an indication of respondents' orientation, while the analyses on energy and the specialists' observations concern different aspects. These elements alone do not establish either a measure of the health damage or the absence of any savings. Likewise, the difficulty of demonstrating the energy benefits does not erase the objective for which daylight saving time was introduced.
The picture presented is therefore that of a custom still in force, challenged because of possible sleep disturbances and energy benefits that are difficult to prove. The source describes the return to standard time, calls for abolition, and the positions of critics, but does not report a decision already adopted to eliminate the time change. In the text, the certain fact remains the moving of the hands of the clock at three and the switch to Central European Time.

item.title: Akira hackers steal data of 100.000 federal employees from Publica
item.description: Over 100,000 federal employees affected Data also relating to partners and children The attack on an external provider dates back to late September
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - More than 100’000 federal employees affected - Data also relating to partners and children - The attack on an external supplier dates back to late September - Akira threatens to publish or sell the data
## Key facts - What → Information theft affecting Publica - Who → Akira hacker group - Scope → Over 100’000 people - When → Late September - Data → Names, dates of birth, addresses, salaries and phone numbers - Threat → Publication or sale of the data - Development → The true scope emerged on Tuesday - RUAG precedent → It had decided to pay after the attack on the US subsidiary
The 11.00 news bulletin on October 21, 2026 reports that the information theft affecting Publica is more serious than expected. Akira’s hackers obtained the personal data of nearly all federal employees of the Confederation: over 100’000 people, including both those still working and those no longer employed by the Confederation.
The list includes officials, judges and even secret agents, as well as former federal councillors. The cyberattack targeted an external provider and dates back to late September. It had already been known for a couple of weeks, but its true scale emerged on Tuesday through articles published by media outlets in the Tamedia group.
### The data and the hackers’ demand The information in the criminals’ possession includes contact details — addresses and phone numbers —, personal details such as names and dates of birth, salary data and additional information concerning partners and children. The source does not describe a simple contact list: it brings together personal details, contact details, remuneration and family-related data.
The hackers are reportedly demanding payment of a ransom. Otherwise, they threaten to publish or sell the data. Publica has reportedly not yet informed those affected about the payment demand; in the meantime, some have already been targeted by attempted scams. ## The scope described by the report The case can be viewed through two dimensions that the report makes explicit: who is included in the group and what types of information were stolen. The first goes beyond the scope of active employees, because the theft also concerns people who are no longer employed by the Confederation. The second goes beyond basic identification: alongside names appear dates of birth, addresses, telephone numbers and salary data.
The text also mentions partners and children. The reference to the data, therefore, does not stop at the individual person included in the list. The categories indicated can be reordered as follows:
### The categories of information indicated | Area | Reported information | |---|---| | Identity | Names and dates of birth | | Contact details | Addresses and telephone numbers | | Compensation | Salary data | | Family | Information relating to partners and children |
The distinction between active employees and former employees is relevant to describing the extent of the theft, but the source does not provide a numerical breakdown between the two groups. The same applies to the occupational categories: we know that officials, judges, secret agents and former federal councillors are mentioned, but not how many belong to each group.
The available figure remains the aggregate one: more than 100’000 people, described as practically all federal employees. The list of professions serves to describe the variety of the group, not to establish a ranking or a specific figure for each role. The wording concerning family members is also limited: the report refers to other information relating to partners and children, without specifying what it is or how many people it concerns. ## The sequence of events in the case and Akira's precedents The service dates the cyberattack to the end of September and reports that it had already been known about for a couple of weeks. On Tuesday, articles published by the Tamedia group's outlets made its actual scope clear. The news report does not provide a precise day for the attack and does not identify the external provider affected: these are the limitations of the available chronological and operational reconstruction.
The passage concerning communication with the people affected is also documented. Regarding the payment demand, Publica has reportedly not yet informed those concerned. The report does state, however, that some people have already been targeted by attempted scams. It does not indicate how many there are or describe the technique used in the attempts.
### The precedent in Switzerland Akira has already carried out attacks in Switzerland, including against private companies. A year ago, the federal authorities urged companies not to comply with the hackers' demands. A few months later, RUAG, owned by the Confederation, had opted to pay, following Akira's attack against its US subsidiary.
This precedent offers a documented but limited comparison: it concerns RUAG and its US subsidiary, not Publica. In the case of the Confederation's pension fund, the source speaks of a ransom demand and threats of publication or sale, but does not indicate the amount requested or any decision on payment.
The material reported by the news service thus makes it possible to clarify the groups involved, the categories of data listed, the presence of a ransom demand and the precedent of RUAG. It does not, however, make it possible to add a numerical breakdown of the groups concerned, details about the external provider or further information about the attempted scams.

On 9 November 2026, in Bern, the National Council for Poverty Issues will hold its first press conference. The event is scheduled from 10.00 to 11.00 at Generationenhaus, Bahnhofplatz 2. The external communication published on 21 October 2026 sets out three objectives for the meeting: present the Council, explain its role and approach, and then outline its priorities.
### The announced mandate The Council is a component of the national framework for preventing and combating poverty. In 2024, the Federal Council approved the creation of this framework. The text also defines the Council as an independent body and as the voice of people with experience of poverty.
The function described in the source is to represent the interests of these people to the public, authorities and organisations. An inauguration event will also take place on the afternoon of 9 November, attended by professionals and political figures. The announcement does not add any other items to the programme. ## From the decision to the presentation
The schedule distinguishes the Federal Council's decision from the first press conference of the National Council for Poverty Issues. In 2024, the creation of the national structure was approved; on November 9, 2026, the body's role, along with its approach and priorities, will instead be presented.
### The documented sequence | Moment | Documented information | |---|---| | 2024 | The Federal Council approved the creation of the national structure. | | October 21, 2026 | The external communication about the event was published. | | November 9, 2026, morning | The first press conference will be held from 10.00 to 11.00. | | November 9, 2026, afternoon | An opening event is planned. |
Comparing the dates avoids a misunderstanding: the 2024 decision concerns the creation of the structure, while the 2026 event concerns the presentation of the Council. The source does not say that the conference approves new measures or changes rules. It documents an occasion dedicated to making explicit the role, approach and priorities of a body defined as independent.
No data are reported on the number of people experiencing poverty, on the results already achieved by the structure or on the effects of the Council's activities. The verifiable relationship between the two moments is therefore institutional and temporal: from the approval of the structure in 2024 to the first presentation announced for November 9, 2026. ## The announced scope
The mandate emerges from those represented. The source describes a precise sequence: people with experience of poverty, an independent Council, then dialogue with public opinion, authorities and organizations. This wording clarifies whom the Council intends to represent, but does not indicate how the people represented are selected or how relations with the various interlocutors are organized.

For the inauguration event, the presence of professional operators and political figures is indicated, but no names, roles, number of participants or precise time are provided.
The communication also does not specify the composition of the Council, the tools with which its approach will be developed, the subsequent deadlines or the content of the priorities that will be presented. These elements remain outside the available text and cannot be added to the announcement.
The confirmed information is the event scheduled for 9 November 2026 in Bern: the first press conference at the Generationenhaus in the morning and an inauguration event in the afternoon. The source thus presents the mandate and the schedule, without anticipating any further decisions or results.

item.title: Tox Info Suisse: mandatory co-financing for industry
item.description: The Federal Council wants to impose co-financing for Tox Info Suisse Chemical and pharmaceutical industries involved Consultation planned until mid.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Council wants to impose co-financing of Tox Info Suisse - The chemical and pharmaceutical industries are involved - Consultation planned until mid-February - Approximately 5'500 chemical and 300 pharmaceutical companies affected
## Key facts - Subject → co-financing of Tox Info Suisse - Sectors → chemicals and medicines - Companies involved → around 5'500 in chemicals and around 300 in medicines - Average annual costs → around 240 francs and almost 5'300 francs - Consultation → until mid-February
BERN - The Federal Council wants the national poison information service, 145, not to be funded exclusively by the public sector. To achieve this objective, it intends to amend the Chemicals Act and the Therapeutic Products Act, so as to require the chemical and pharmaceutical industries to co-finance Tox Info Suisse.
The project was confirmed in a statement issued on Wednesday after the government meeting. The text states that the chemical and pharmaceutical industries are unwilling to provide lasting and substantial support for the service on a voluntary basis. According to the statement, this position emerged in discussions between the Federal Department of Home Affairs (FDHA) and delegations from the two sectors.
The Federal Council justifies the obligation by citing the role of producers in poisonings. Producers in the two sectors are identified as direct and indirect contributors to more than 70% of poisonings that occur every year in Switzerland. For the government, this link justifies the industry's financial involvement.
The Federal Council will submit the amendments for consultation until mid-February. According to the data provided, the future obligation would concern around 5'500 companies in the chemicals sector and around 300 companies in the medicines sector.
The text also indicates the average annual costs: around 240 francs for producers of chemicals and almost 5'300 francs for holders of medicinal product authorizations. The difference between the two figures reflects the distinction between the two groups concerned.
### The point announced in Bern The decision described by the source is a regulatory intention: the Federal Council wants to shift the model from one that is not exclusively publicly funded to mandatory co-financing by the two sectors. The step indicated now is consultation on the two laws; the text does not yet report an outcome of the procedure. ## Comparison of the number of entities and the average contribution
The proposal brings together two very different numbers: on the one hand, the larger number of companies in the chemical sector, and on the other, the smaller group of holders of authorizations for medicinal products. Each category is associated with a different average annual cost.
### Two calculation bases To make the data comparable, the number of entities indicated by the government can be multiplied by the corresponding average annual cost. The result is an arithmetic calculation based on the source values, not a sum presented directly in the federal note.
| Sector | Entities indicated | Average annual cost | Indicative calculation | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Chemical substances | approximately 5'500 companies | approximately 240 francs | approximately 1,32 million francs | | Medicinal products | approximately 300 authorization holders | almost 5'300 francs | almost 1,59 million francs |
In the chemical sector, 5'500 multiplied by 240 produces 1'320'000 francs, that is, approximately 1,32 million. In the medicinal products sector, 300 multiplied by 5'300 produces 1'590'000 francs, that is, almost 1,59 million. The arithmetic sum is therefore approximately 2,91 million francs per year, if it is assumed that each entity falls within the indicated average cost.
However, this sum is not a figure announced by the Federal Council. It serves only to consider the number of companies and the average contribution together, while keeping the annual period visible. The individual ratio also shows a clear difference: almost 5'300 francs is equivalent to approximately 22 times 240 francs. The comparison must nevertheless remain indicative, because the source values are expressed as averages.
The available figures thus show two levels: the chemical sector includes more companies, but with a lower average cost per producer; the medicinal products sector includes fewer holders, with a higher average cost. The source does not describe the formula by which the individual amount would be calculated, nor the actual revenue from the new regulation. ## The precedent for public funding
The federal proposal is part of a funding history dating back about sixty years. Initially, Tox Info Suisse could rely on support from private organizations and on revenue secured through contracts with hospitals, donations and public contributions. In recent years, however, most private organizations have progressively withdrawn their support.
### From the historical model to parliamentary debate The withdrawal of private funders is the point that the Federal Council highlighted in talks with industry. The note states that the voluntary support of the two sectors does not appear sufficient to guarantee lasting and substantial support for the poison-case advisory service.
Parliament had already addressed the issue: during the 2025 winter session, it had allocated the resources needed to ensure the continuity of the national emergency number for poisonings, but the Federal Council had rejected the increase.
Speaking in the Council of States, Federal Councillor Karin Keller-Sutter had warned that Parliament’s approval of the increase in federal funds would reduce the Confederation’s negotiating room. According to reports, the government aimed to obtain co-financing for Tox Info from private organizations. Keller-Sutter had also reported that the Federal Council considered the withdrawal of private organizations from the emergency service regrettable.
### What remains open The available content does not specify the precise closing date of the consultation, its outcome or the date on which the amendments will enter into force. Nor does it explain how the costs would be distributed among the individual companies or how average values would be converted into an individual amount.
The source therefore presents a proposal submitted for consultation, not a regulation that has already entered into force. It reports the parliamentary funding secured for the continuation of the service and the Federal Council’s intention to make the two sectors participate on a mandatory basis, but does not document any further changes to the operation of number 145.

item.title: Civil protection: Bern plans to deploy civilian service personnel
item.description: From January, civil service personnel will be able to work in civil protection The Federal Council amends the implementing ordinances As of January 1
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Starting in January, civilian service personnel will be able to serve in civil protection - The Federal Council amends the implementing ordinances - As of January 1, 2025, civil protection had 57'000 personnel - The target set for civil protection is 72'000 personnel
## Key facts - Decision: Federal Council - Addressees: cantonal civil protection organizations - Condition: deployment when regular personnel are insufficient - Civil protection figures: 57'000 personnel against a target of 72'000 - Outlook: approximately 4'500 recruits per year and 50'000 personnel by 2030 if the trend does not change
The Federal Council approved the ordinance amendments that will allow, from January, persons required to perform civilian service to be deployed in cantonal civil protection organizations. The measure is intended to fill cantonal gaps when regular personnel are insufficient.
The source reports that the measures had been presented and sent out for consultation in November 2025. The stated aim is to strengthen civil protection personnel, also referred to in the text by the abbreviation PC.
### The government's decision
The figure reported for January 1, 2025, is 57'000 active personnel, against a target set at 72'000. The source also indicates annual recruitment of approximately 4'500 people and notes that, if the trend does not change, the stated recruitment would bring the number of personnel to 50'000 by 2030. The use of civilian service personnel is therefore included in a measure linked to shortages in civil protection at the cantonal level.
Following Parliament's approval, in March last year, of the partial revision of the Population and Civil Protection Act (LPPC), the Federal Council adjusted the ordinances concerned. According to the note, the changes are primarily organizational and administrative in nature and concern the Cantons first and foremost. ## The numerical gap indicated by the source
The comparison between the two main values produces a difference of 15'000 personnel: 72'000, the target set, minus 57'000 actual personnel recorded as of January 1, 2025. This is an arithmetic calculation based on the reported data, not a new figure communicated by the Federal Council.
| Indicator | Reported data | |---|---:| | Actual personnel as of January 1, 2025 | 57'000 | | Target set | 72'000 | | Annual recruitment | approximately 4'500 personnel | | Projection indicated | 50'000 personnel by 2030, if the trend does not change |
The overview compares a snapshot, that of January 1, 2025, with a numerical target and a conditional projection. The source does not present the figure of 50'000 as a result already achieved: it links it to the assumption that the trend remains unchanged. The recruitment of approximately 4'500 personnel is also indicated as an annual figure, without further details on its composition.
### From cantonal shortages to the deployment of civilian service personnel
The source places the deployment of civilian service personnel in cases where regular personnel are insufficient; it does not present it as a general measure unrelated to cantonal shortages. To make this transition possible, civil protection organizations will be recognized as institutions where civilian service can be performed.
The project also supplements the decision with operational rules: deployment procedures, the rights and duties of civilian service personnel, and allocation criteria. The stated priority is residence and language, according to the same criterion provided for personnel. The territorial dimension is therefore explicitly present both in the place where the shortage is identified and in the order of allocation described by the source.
The text also provides criteria for calculating the authorized staffing level and mechanisms for addressing shortages. These are elements of the approved rules, not a description of operational results already measured in the cantons. ## From the revision of the LPPC to the ordinances
The federal measure comes after two steps indicated in the source. The measures had been presented and submitted for consultation in November 2025; in March last year, Parliament had approved the partial revision of the LPPC. The Federal Council adapted the ordinances to implement those changes.
The package includes the ordinances relating to civil protection, civilian service, the processing of civilian service data, military information systems and DDPS information systems. According to the note, the measures are primarily organizational and administrative in nature and mainly affect the cantons.
### What is regulated
The most concrete part of the project concerns how civilian service personnel may be deployed. The procedures must be defined together with the rights and duties of persons required to perform civilian service. Priority assignment based on place of residence and language is indicated as a rule analogous to that used for military personnel.
The framework also establishes the criteria for calculating the authorized strength, provides mechanisms for addressing shortages and provides for a reduction in basic training for civil protection volunteers. Overall, these provisions outline an administrative intervention that goes beyond merely enabling civilian service personnel to be deployed in cantonal organizations.
### The limits of the available data
The source does not quantify how many civilian service personnel will be deployed, does not distribute the assignments among the individual cantons and does not indicate a duration for the assignments. Nor does it report any results following the start of the measure. Therefore, the figure of 50'000 military personnel by 2030 remains, in the text, a projection tied to the condition that the trend does not change; it is not presented as a certain outcome.
The documented picture is limited: a decision by the Federal Council, a partial revision approved by Parliament and a set of changes aimed primarily at cantonal organization. The source contains no individual statements by members of the government or cantonal authorities, nor any additional figures on implementation.

item.title: Competitiveness package: over 90% implemented or underway
item.description: More than 90% of the 60 measures have been implemented or are being implemented.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - More than 90% of the 60 measures have been implemented or are being implemented. - 16 measures are in force and 39 are being implemented. - The package aims to reduce regulatory burdens for businesses. - At least 20% of Swiss companies can benefit from the relief.
## Key facts - What → package for the competitiveness of the Swiss economy - Status → 16 measures in force, 39 being implemented, 5 not implemented or partial - Estimated beneficiaries → at least 20% of companies in Switzerland - Time frame → just under one year after adoption - Source → Federal Council; news reported by Keystone-ATS
Just under one year after adoption, the package for the competitiveness of the Swiss economy presents, according to the report adopted by the Federal Council, a positive balance. More than 90% of the 60 measures have already been implemented or are being implemented. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS.
The stated objective is to ease the regulatory burdens currently weighing on businesses and limit additional ones as much as possible. In the executive's statement, the estimate of the number of beneficiaries indicates that these relief measures could affect at least one in five companies in Switzerland. The measures concern different sectors and obligations, as shown by the distinction between those already introduced and those still being implemented.
### The report at a glance
The breakdown is precise: 16 measures are already in force, while 39 are being implemented. Five, on the other hand, have not been implemented so far or have only been implemented in part. Adding the first two categories gives 55 measures out of 60, a proportion consistent with the phrase “more than 90%” used in the report.
The Federal Council thus distinguishes between what is already operational and what is still progressing. For the five measures not implemented or only partially implemented, the available text does not indicate their names or provide a timeline. The positive balance reported by Keystone-ATS therefore concerns the package as a whole, while the details show that the process is not complete for all 60 measures. ## Measures under implementation
The report does not focus the measures on a single requirement. The part still under implementation covers imports, taxation and packaging, with different estimated groups affected. The comparison below brings together only the figures indicated in the source.
### Figures and requirements
| Area | Measure indicated | Group affected or figure | |---|---|---| | Timber from the EU | Simplifications for importing | approximately 36 000 importers | | VAT | Annual settlement instead of quarterly | 25 000 businesses | | Annual accounts | Abolition of the obligation to submit them | approximately 45 000 companies | | Beverage packaging | New rules reducing burdens | approximately 35 000 companies |
The first comparison concerns frequency: for 25 000 businesses, VAT settlement may change from quarterly to annual. The report presents this measure as a future possibility because it includes it among those under implementation. The figure therefore concerns the settlement frequency indicated in the source.
A second comparison concerns the group affected. The simplifications for importing timber from the EU are associated with approximately 36 000 importers, while the new rules on beverage packaging are indicated as capable of reducing burdens for approximately 35 000 companies. The two figures are on almost the same numerical scale, but refer to different measures and activities.
The same criterion applies to the approximately 45 000 companies for which the obligation to submit annual accounts will be abolished. The source therefore provides separate figures, useful for understanding the scope of the individual measures, without presenting them as an overall total of companies. The package thus combines import simplifications, a different VAT frequency, and the reduction or abolition of specific requirements. ## Measures already introduced and limitations of the overview
The report cites three groups of measures already introduced: relief measures for the aviation sector, climate compensation initiatives and road-signage works. In the first case, the intervals between inspections have been extended for a number of companies that may be as high as 500. For the 184 climate compensation projects, reporting can now be completed within four years.
Road signage also falls among the operational measures: under certain conditions, night and Sunday work is possible without authorization. The wording does not eliminate every requirement: the report expressly links this possibility to compliance with conditions, without specifying them in the available text.
Reading the overview therefore requires keeping three pieces of information separate: the overall share, the status of the individual measures and the estimated number of beneficiaries. More than 90% has been implemented or is being implemented, but five measures have not been implemented or have been implemented only partially. At least 20%, meanwhile, is the estimated share of companies in Switzerland that can benefit from the relief; it is not a share referring only to aviation, VAT or packaging.
The report does not provide a single total for the companies involved. The groups listed for importers, companies and aviation companies are associated with different measures, and the text does not clarify any overlaps. Nor does it identify the five measures that remained unimplemented or partial. These are the informational limitations of the overview reported by the Federal Council.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/cf%3a-pacchetto-competitivit%c3%a0-economia%2c-bilancio-positivo/92249999)*

item.title: Tamedia, over 100 take to the streets in Zurich against 34 full-time job cuts
item.description: More than 100 employees protest in Zurich Tamedia announces 34 fewer full-time positions The cuts affect 41 employees Workers call for investment
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Over 100 employees protest in Zurich - Tamedia announces 34 fewer full-time positions - The cuts affect 41 employees - Workers call for investment in journalism
## Key facts - Location → Tamedia headquarters, Werdstrasse in Zurich - When → Tuesday at noon - Jobs eliminated → 34 full-time - Employees affected → 41 - Affected newsrooms → newsrooms in German-speaking Switzerland and French-speaking Switzerland - Support → Raphael Golta, president of the city of Zurich (SP) - Request → consultation also in German-speaking Switzerland
On Tuesday at noon, more than 100 Tamedia employees gathered outside the publishing house's headquarters on Werdstrasse in Zurich. The demonstration protested the layoffs announced in recent weeks. The workers called for an immediate halt to the job cuts, also receiving support from Raphael Golta, president of the city of Zurich and a member of the SP.
Speaking in front of the workers, Golta recalled his connection to the Zurich daily newspaper. He explained that he reads it every morning to follow events around the world. The former journalist said he was concerned about the future of local journalism and declared that he wanted to continue reading articles written by professionals rather than produced by artificial intelligence systems.
### The newsrooms' demands
The company management came under fire during the mobilization. According to the newsrooms, the consequences of wrong decisions and ineffective strategies systematically fell on employees. Another point criticized was the progressive reduction in resources available for editorial work. Among the signs displayed was the slogan «Journalism instead of AI», which sums up the demand to invest in the work of information professionals.
Staff from Tamedia's French-speaking Switzerland newsrooms also joined the mobilization. On Tuesday, the French-speaking colleagues sent the Zurich employees affected by the cuts a letter expressing solidarity.
About two weeks ago, the company announced the elimination of 34 full-time positions in the newsrooms of German-speaking Switzerland and French-speaking Switzerland; the measure will lead to 41 employees being laid off. Staff are now asking that the consultation procedure, already planned in French-speaking Switzerland, also be extended to German-speaking Switzerland. ## What the numbers indicate
The employment situation involves two different quantities, which the source presents separately: 34 full-time jobs and 41 employees affected by the layoffs. The distinction is relevant because one number indicates positions, while the other indicates people. The two figures are therefore not interchangeable.
| Item | Reported figure | |---|---| | Jobs eliminated | 34 full-time | | Employees affected | 41 | | Editorial areas | Newsrooms in German-speaking Switzerland and French-speaking Switzerland | | Announcement | About two weeks before the protest |
Purely arithmetically, the difference between 41 and 34 is 7 units. However, the text does not explain the composition of this difference and does not make it possible to determine how many people correspond to each full-time position. The figure only makes it possible to keep distinct the number of positions indicated in the plan and the number of employees who, according to Tamedia, will be laid off.
The geographical scope also has two documented levels. The protest took place in Zurich, while the plan concerns the newsrooms of German-speaking Switzerland and French-speaking Switzerland. French-speaking staff members also took part in the mobilization and distributed a letter of solidarity. The news item therefore describes a labor dispute involving both main linguistic areas mentioned in the text, without providing a breakdown of the 34 positions or the 41 employees between the two regions.
The demands likewise fall into two areas. On the employment front, the workers call for an end to the cuts, a consultation procedure also in German-speaking Switzerland, and consideration of voluntary departures. On the editorial front, they call for greater investment in journalism carried out by professionals rather than entrusted to artificial intelligence. These are staff demands: the source does not report that they have already been accepted by management. ## The support and what remains to be clarified
The protest is not described solely as a mobilization within the newsrooms. Raphael Golta, president of the City of Zurich, addressed the workers, expressing support for the employees and concern about the future of local news. His reference to the Zurich daily and to reading the newspaper every day is presented together with the request to continue reading articles written by professionals. The text therefore documents support expressed during the demonstration, but does not attribute decisions on layoffs or Tamedia's strategies to the City of Zurich.
### Information not yet available
Solidarity from French-speaking Switzerland is another element reported by the source. Some French-speaking staff members took part in the mobilization and circulated a letter on Tuesday in support of their Zurich colleagues. However, neither the precise number of French-speaking participants nor the full content of the letter is indicated.
The accusations against management are attributed to the editorial teams: the employees criticize the adoption of decisions they consider wrong and strategies they describe as ineffective, arguing that the consequences fall on workers. The text does not report a response from company management to these accusations. It also does not indicate how the 34 eliminated positions would be distributed between German-speaking Switzerland and French-speaking Switzerland, nor does it provide individual details about the 41 employees involved.
The issue of artificial intelligence should also be kept within the limits described. AI is at the center of the slogans and calls for greater investment in professional journalism, but the source does not claim that artificial intelligence is the cause of the layoffs or that it has replaced specific roles.
The text uses relative time references, such as Tuesday and about two weeks ago, without specifying a calendar date. The outcome of the consultation procedure is not reported; it does not say whether the cuts were modified, and no further measures after the protest are indicated.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1957983/zurigo-dipendenti-svizzera-tamedia-licenziamenti-ia)*

item.title: System failure: Swiss air capacity at 50%
item.description: Technical failure in Skyguide systems Tuesday afternoon Skyguide operates at 50% capacity as a precaution Takeoffs and landings briefly suspended
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Technical malfunction in Skyguide systems Tuesday afternoon - Skyguide operates at 50% capacity as a precaution - Takeoffs and landings briefly suspended in Zurich and Geneva - Cyberattack ruled out; operations then resumed
## Key facts - When → Tuesday afternoon - Who → Skyguide - Problem → malfunction of the system that generates the radar image - Capacity → 50% as a precaution - Airports → Zurich and Geneva
### The air traffic system failure
On Tuesday afternoon, a technical problem affected Skyguide's systems, causing disruptions to Swiss air traffic. Tages-Anzeiger was the first to report the news: at Zurich Airport, some flights were grounded.
Takeoffs and landings at the airports in Zurich and Geneva were temporarily suspended. The interruption was brief, and operations then resumed at both airports. Skyguide nevertheless confirmed that it was operating at 50% of its capacity, a precautionary measure.
According to the company's statement, the reduction in capacity was caused by a failure in the system that provides controllers with a radar representation of air traffic. The statement also ruled out a cyberattack and assured that safety in Swiss airspace was guaranteed.
> “Safety in Swiss airspace is guaranteed.”
Skyguide warned that reduced capacity could lead to delays. The text does not indicate the number of flights involved, the exact duration of the suspension or the number of delays recorded.
The company said it had mobilized a crisis team and intended to restore service as soon as possible, limiting the repercussions for air traffic. Skyguide also apologized to its partners and passengers. ## What the 50% figure means
The figure reported by Skyguide measures operational capacity; the source does not include a count of cancelled flights. The wording of the 50% figure does not, by itself, amount to a statistic on flights: the note refers to operations at 50% as a precaution. It is not documented how many connections were affected or whether the effect was the same for all of them.
The figure should be read together with the other points in the communication. On the one hand, takeoffs and landings in Zurich and Geneva were briefly suspended; on the other, operations resumed. Skyguide nevertheless indicated that delays were possible with reduced capacity. The source does not provide a precise time for the start or end of the suspension and does not quantify the impact on passengers.
### The role of the radar image
The problem affected the system responsible for providing controllers with a radar representation of air traffic. The note explicitly links this malfunction to the decision to reduce operational capacity and rules out a cyberattack as its cause.
| Element | Reported figure | |---|---| | Capacity | 50% as a precaution | | Takeoffs and landings | Briefly suspended, then resumed | | Airports named | Zurich and Geneva | | Possible effect | Delays | | Safety | Guaranteed in Swiss airspace |
This reading makes it possible to distinguish three aspects that may overlap in news reports: the temporary suspension of operations, reduced capacity, and possible delays. The source confirms all three, but does not indicate how many flights departed, how many remained on the ground, or how long they waited. For this reason, the 50% should be presented as the capacity level reported by Skyguide, not as a complete statistic on flights or passengers. ## Restoration and information still missing
Skyguide's communication describes a two-stage process. First, the precautionary reduction in capacity, followed by the resumption of operations at Zurich and Geneva airports. In parallel, the company activated a crisis team to address the service disruption and limit the impact on air traffic.
Skyguide stated that it aims to restore full capacity in the coming hours. The source therefore reports an operational objective, but does not state that full restoration has already occurred. This is also why the warning about possible delays after takeoffs and landings resume remains.
### What the statement confirms
The press release makes it possible to establish some points without extending them beyond the available data. The problem is defined as a malfunction of the system that generates the radar image; safety in Swiss airspace is stated to be guaranteed; a cyberattack is ruled out; operations at the two airports mentioned have resumed. Skyguide also conveys its apologies to partners and passengers.
The name of the technical component affected, the exact time of the failure, the overall duration of the limitation, the number of flights left on the ground, the number of passengers involved and the possible extent of the delays remain undocumented. The source does not quantify any possible costs or economic consequences for airports, airlines or travelers.
The geographical scope of the news is equally precise: the airports of Zurich and Geneva are named, but no data are provided on other airports. The company speaks of a solution as soon as possible and of an impact to be reduced to a minimum; no official time for the completion of restoration is reported. The available update, therefore, is that capacity is limited to 50% as a precaution, with operations resumed and delays still possible.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/attualita/1957991/zurigo-skyguide-aereo-capacita-guasto-spazio)*

item.title: Finma approves the first Swiss Bitcoin ETF
item.description: Finma authorizes the first direct public Bitcoin fund The fund is traded on the stock exchange The decision follows growing interest
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Finma authorizes the first public fund invested directly in Bitcoin - The fund is traded on an exchange - The decision follows growing interest in cryptocurrencies - Market risk remains very high
## Key facts - Authority → Finma - Instrument → first public fund that invests directly in Bitcoin - Market → exchange-traded fund - Interest → cryptocurrencies, particularly Bitcoin - Risk → very high
### The first authorization In Zurich, Finma authorized a fund open to the public that invests directly in Bitcoin, the first of its kind. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the authority justified the decision by citing the growing interest in cryptocurrency investments, especially in Bitcoin.
For the first time, Finma explains, this is a publicly traded fund for the public that invests directly in the cryptocurrency. The product is referred to in the text as a Bitcoin ETF. The decision therefore concerns an instrument intended for the public and traded on the stock market, not merely an announcement about investors' interest.
Finma assumes that the approval may increase investor protection. At the same time, the authority highlights the risk associated with investments in Bitcoin and accompanies the authorization with an explicit reminder to exercise caution regarding market risk.
The protection indicated in the statement also stems from the measures required of supervised institutions. These must reduce operational risks and custody-related risks. According to Finma, applying the rules of conduct contributes to greater protection compared with direct investments in cryptocurrencies.
The news therefore contains two distinct elements: the authorization of the first publicly traded fund with direct investment in Bitcoin and the obligation for supervised institutions to adopt measures concerning operational and custody risks. In the same statement, however, Finma keeps the warning about cryptocurrency risk at the forefront. ## Two aspects not to be confused
### Operational safeguards and market risk Finma's communication separates investor protection from the risk associated with Bitcoin's performance. The first aspect concerns how supervised institutions must organize the management of the investment, reducing operational risks and those related to custody. The second, by contrast, concerns the value of the invested capital, which is exposed to the sharp fluctuations of cryptocurrencies.
| Aspect | Finma's indication | |---|---| | Instrument | Public investment fund, traded on an exchange and invested directly in Bitcoin | | Operational risks | Supervised institutions must take measures to reduce them | | Custody risks | Institutions must also take specific measures regarding this aspect | | Comparison | Conduct rules offer greater protection compared with direct investment in cryptocurrencies | | Market | The risk associated with Bitcoin remains very high, even through an approved ETF |
The relationship between these elements is the most useful aspect of the decision. Operational and custody measures can strengthen the protection provided to those who access the fund, but Finma does not present the approval as eliminating market risk. On the contrary, it defines investments in Bitcoin as highly risky even when they are made through an authorized ETF.
For the Swiss public, the documented new feature is therefore the existence of an investment channel available to the public and traded on an exchange, with direct investment in Bitcoin. The comparison with direct investment does not concern a promise of return, but the level of protection associated with the conduct rules applied by supervised institutions.
Finma also draws attention to the effect of fluctuations on capital. According to the statement, this aspect must be taken into account in the investment decision, especially in relation to the size of the amount invested. The distinction remains clear: the authorization concerns the structure and safeguards of the investment, while Bitcoin's market risk remains very high. ## The scope of the news
### No provider identified Finma's statement does not mention a specific ETF provider. At the request of the news agency AWP, a spokesperson explained that several fund providers had submitted or announced applications. The authority, however, does not comment further on the ongoing authorization procedures.
This leaves the main fact established, but does not attribute the product to a specific company. The source documents the first authorization of a public investment fund that invests directly in Bitcoin and clarifies that the fund is traded on an exchange. It does not, however, indicate which of the various providers submitted the authorized product.
The informational limitation is accompanied by a very precise warning about risk. Finma does not reduce the issue to the custody or organization of institutions: it also draws attention to the market risk directly associated with Bitcoin and defines it as very high. The assessment also applies to an approved ETF.
The clearest part of the warning is this:
> Strong fluctuations in cryptocurrencies can significantly reduce the value of the invested capital.
Finma therefore classifies investments in Bitcoin as highly risky, including those made through the new ETF. In the statement, the amount invested is identified as an element to be taken into consideration in the investment decision. No numerical threshold is provided, and no expected return is presented.
The verifiable picture thus remains limited: Switzerland has authorized for the first time a public fund traded on an exchange that invests directly in Bitcoin; supervised institutions must take measures regarding operational and custody risks; market risk remains very high, and the provider's name has not been disclosed.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/economia/1957927/bitcoin-investimenti-etf-primo-finma)*

item.title: Workplace harassment in SMEs: the data and the KMU konkret+ project
item.description: Since COVID, reports in Swiss SMEs have increased.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Since COVID-19, reports in Swiss SMEs have increased. - 44% of women report harassment at work. - The harasser often holds a position of power. - Eight services are launching the KMU konkret+ project.
## Key facts - Period → since COVID-19 - Women affected → 44% at least once during their careers - Men affected → 17% at least once during their careers - Companies most at risk → small and medium-sized enterprises - People most at risk → apprentices, new hires and workers in insecure employment - Project → KMU konkret+ - Target audience → companies with up to 250 employees
On October 20, 2026, the source reported a sharp increase in sexual harassment at work in small and medium-sized enterprises following the pandemic and with the return to the office. The observation comes from the equal opportunities offices of German-speaking Switzerland and is also reported by the Berner Zeitung.
Yet the phenomenon is more widespread than one might imagine: according to a study by the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (Seco), 44% of women and 17% of men have experienced sexual harassment at work at least once during their careers. Moreover, one employee in five would like their company to do more.
### A problem related to power relations
> “Harassment is still too often passed off as a flirt that went wrong or a distasteful compliment.”
Voloder observes that it is not only the harasser’s intention that matters: the consequences for the victim and the work group must also be considered. It is often someone with greater power, whether a supervisor, colleague or customer.
The source describes apprentices, new hires and workers in insecure employment as the most at risk. In these conditions, people subjected to harassing behavior may prefer to remain silent, especially when they believe that the person responsible is unlikely to face consequences. The picture presented therefore concerns both the prevalence of the phenomenon and the way hierarchical relationships can affect the possibility of speaking out and reacting. ## What the data and procedures show
The comparison between the Seco data is clear: 44% of women and 17% of men report having experienced sexual harassment at work at least once during their careers. The difference is 27 percentage points. This is a comparison between two groups over the same time period, not a change recorded from one year to the next. The cited study is not presented as a ranking among sectors or as a measure of SMEs alone.
Alongside these percentages is another indicator: one in five employees believes that their company should do more. The source places it alongside the figure for the people involved, showing that the issue concerns both those who experience harassment and the organizational response of companies.
### Two aspects to be assessed separately
Victims can take action under employment law and criminal law. The article does, however, identify a company practice considered wrong: waiting for a judgment before taking measures. The two procedures, according to Voloder, must be assessed separately. The source does not establish an automatic link between a report and dismissal, nor does it present every ill-judged remark as sufficient grounds for ending an employment relationship.
For those who report, the text identifies evidence as decisive. The elements mentioned include messages, chat conversations, and detailed notes about what happened, specifying when and where it occurred. Thus, no single form of documentation is indicated, but rather a series of traces that can reconstruct the incident.
The everyday conduct of managers is also identified as part of the response. A policy posted on a bulletin board is not enough if those in charge then use vulgar language. Managers must intervene immediately and set a good example. Colleagues, on the other hand, can show concern by asking the person involved whether they would like to talk about it. If someone realizes that they have offended another person, the conduct indicated by the source is to apologize and not repeat the behavior. ## The sectors mentioned and the response for SMEs
The Zeitung article focuses primarily on three sectors in which the issue is more pronounced due to the lack of prevention bodies: construction, industry and the hospitality sector. The source does not assign specific percentages to these areas or establish which records the highest number of cases. It presents them as sectors mentioned in the discussion of preventive shortcomings.
### KMU konkret+
To fill the gap, the KMU konkret+ project was launched by eight equal-opportunity offices in German-speaking Switzerland, including that of the Canton of Bern. The initiative offers training, model regulations and advice to companies with up to 250 employees.
The project therefore directly targets the companies identified by the source as most at risk of neglecting the issue: SMEs. Its scope is defined both by the tools made available and by the size limit specified for the target companies. The source does not, however, provide data on companies’ participation, results already achieved or any reduction in reports following the launch.
The geographical context must be understood by distinguishing the article’s different references. The phenomenon is described as widespread throughout Switzerland, and the study’s data come from Seco. The observations on the increase in reports and the difficulties faced by companies, however, come from the equal-opportunity offices in German-speaking Switzerland, while the project also includes the office of the Canton of Bern.
No separate figures are provided by canton, sector or company size, nor are individual cases or court decisions described. The influence of positions of power, the greater exposure of apprentices, newly hired employees and precarious workers, and the need—identified by the source—for a corporate response that does not automatically wait until the end of criminal proceedings nevertheless remain documented.
*Source: [tio.ch](https://www.tio.ch/svizzera/attualita/1957721/voloder-molestie-carriera-imprese-vittima)*

item.title: Swiss watches: exports at 2,2 billion in September, +11,7%
item.description: In September 2026, exports rise by 11,7% to 2,2 billion francs; 1,4 million pieces (+19,9%).
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - September 2026: exports worth 2,2 billion francs - Value up 11,7% compared with September 2025 - 1,4 million watches: +19,9% - The United States leads the markets with 293 million
## Key facts | Item | Value | |---|---| | Period | September 2026 | | Location | Bienne (BE) | | Data source | Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry (FH) | | Exports | 2,2 billion francs | | Annual growth in value | 11,7% | | Timepieces exported | 1,4 million | | Growth in number | 19,9% | | First nine months | +2,7%, to 19,5 billion francs |
### The September figure
In September 2026, Swiss watch exports abroad stood at 2,2 billion francs. According to data released by the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry (FH), the value increased by 11,7% compared with the same period in 2025. From Bienne (BE), the source therefore reports growth of over 11%, while the number of timepieces sold rose by 19,9%, reaching 1,4 million.
The arithmetic comparison between 19,9% and 11,7% yields 8,2 percentage points: quantity grew more than value in the monthly data. Both measures are therefore increasing, but the difference between the rates should be interpreted as the gap between growth in the number and growth in value, not as a second export figure.
September's growth follows that of the previous three months, already identified by the source as a confirmed trend: August recorded +9,1%, July +9,6% and June +11,2%. The monthly trajectory also includes May's mini-rebound, +0,4%, after a very difficult April, at -16,6%. Between August and September, the rate rose from +9,1% to +11,7%, an increase of 2,6 percentage points calculated from the stated rates.
Over the January–September period, the balance remains positive: Swiss watch exports rose by 2,7% in value year on year, reaching 19,5 billion francs. The cumulative figure covers the first nine months, while the 2,2 billion concerns September: the two figures therefore refer to different time windows. ## The geography of sales
### Six markets, one shared weight
The overall result does not describe all markets in the same way. For September, the Federation of the Watch Industry pairs sales value with a percentage change for the main markets. The order reported by the source starts with the United States and continues with France, Japan, the United Kingdom, Hong Kong and mainland China.
| Market | September sales | Reported change | |---|---:|---:| | United States | 293 million francs | +85,7% | | France | 247 million francs | +11,1% | | Japan | 177 million francs | +8% | | United Kingdom | 164 million francs | -5,2% | | Hong Kong | 161 million francs | +3% | | Mainland China | 130 million francs | +5,8% |
The first comparison concerns the absolute values given for the month. The difference between the United States and France is 46 million francs, calculated as the difference between 293 and 247 million. The gap between the leading market and mainland China rises to 163 million, obtained by subtracting 130 from 293. These are differences between the listed monthly values, not individual shares of exports.
The second comparison concerns the rates instead. The United States records the highest increase, +85,7%, while France posts +11,1% and Japan +8%. Hong Kong grows by +3% and mainland China by +5,8%; the United Kingdom is the only one of the six markets listed with a negative change, amounting to -5,2%.
The source also specifies that these six markets together account for 53% of sales abroad. The 53% measures the group's combined weight, while the 85,7% measures the change in the United States: the two percentages have different bases and are not directly interchangeable. The reported data do not break down the overall +11,7% among the individual markets, so they do not quantify each one's contribution to total growth. ## Price ranges and limits of the snapshot
### Growth by segment
The second key perspective provided by the source concerns price ranges. In this case, the comparison is expressed in terms of value and comprises four groups: watches under 200 francs, products between 200 and 500 francs, items between 500 and 3000 francs, and timepieces over 3000 francs.
| Price range | Growth in value | |---|---:| | Less than 200 francs | +30,2% | | From 200 to 500 francs | +52,1% | | From 500 to 3000 francs | +11,8% | | Over 3000 francs | +9,9% |
All ranges are growing, but with different intensities. The 200 to 500 franc group has the highest rate, +52,1%, followed by watches under 200 francs, +30,2%. The 500 to 3000 franc range grows by 11,8%, while the range over 3000 francs records +9,9%.
Here too, the numerical comparison adds a useful distinction: between the highest and lowest growth rates there are 42,2 percentage points, calculated as 52,1 minus 9,9. The distance between the 500-3000 segment and the one over 3000 is instead 1,9 points. These calculations concern only the growth rates in value; the source does not provide the absolute amounts exported in each range.
The monthly total of 2,2 billion francs and the overall number of 1,4 million timepieces are not broken down by segment. Therefore, the reported data do not show how many units belong to each range, nor what the average value of a watch is for each group. Likewise, the text does not cross-reference price ranges and geographical markets.
The available snapshot therefore remains limited to export performance: September's growth, the balance for the first nine months, and changes in the segments. The text does not document the causes of the progression, margins, employment, domestic-market sales, or forecasts for the full year. The monthly +11,7% and the +2,7% for the first nine months describe different periods and, on their own, do not allow the result to be projected beyond the data indicated.

The external communication, published in Bern on October 20, 2026, concerns circular letter no. 221, updated as of January 1, 2027, and describes the effects of the adjustment for bracket creep on withholding tax rates and deductions.
### The two figures given The note provides two numerical references. The tax deduction for each child amounts to 264 CHF. Alongside this figure, the text gives the median value of actual employment income as 5'925 CHF per month.
The text uses the word «now», but does not provide the previous value. It is therefore not possible, based on the available content, to measure the extent of the adjustment compared with an earlier period.

The individual rates or tax rates applicable to the different cases are not listed in the text provided. The communication therefore documents the adjustments reported and the two figures given, without a complete table for individual calculation. ## The correct comparison of the data
### Amounts with different units The most robust comparison is not a percentage, but the distinction between the two measures. The amount of 264 CHF is presented as a tax deduction for each child. The 5'925 CHF figure, on the other hand, is the median value of actual employment incomes, and the source expresses it per month. The text does not assign a period to the deduction and does not indicate whether the amount should be understood as monthly, annual, or at another interval. Putting the two amounts into the same ratio would therefore produce an undocumented result.
The term «adjustments» should also be interpreted with caution. The communication explains that they are due to the effects of compensation for bracket creep, but it does not provide a previous value, a formula, or an individual example. The reported value can be identified, but the change for a specific situation cannot be quantified from this note alone.
According to the domain reference associated with the verification, the Swiss tax framework comprises three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal taxes, and municipal taxes. Each canton has its own law and its own multiplier; for municipalities, the multiplier is applied to cantonal tax. This general framework does not add any rates or details to circular no. 221 that the text does not publish. ## Information limitations of the communication

In the available text, it does not specify the rates for individual categories, details for a canton or municipality, or a calculation relating to an individual. This scope makes it possible to report the values, but not to reconstruct an individual tax tariff.
The text contains no separate figures for direct federal tax or VAT, nor any data on AVS/AHV, LPP/BVG, or LAMal/KVG. There are also no cost-of-living indicators or a figure identified as a minimum wage. The figure of 5'925 CHF is defined as the median value of actual employment income, while the deduction of 264 CHF applies to each child: the communication provides no further qualifications.
The dates also have different functions: 20 October 2026 is the publication date, while 1 January 2027 is the status indicated for the circular. The source provides no other comparison periods or subsequent updates. For a separate numerical comparison, the salary and tax calculator is available.
